translationRepairs: Tens of thousands of Hu households in Bing, Dingyang, and Ercheng rose, poured into Pingyang, crowned Cao Hong shanyu, and pillaged widely.

Tens of thousands of Hu households in Bing, Dingyang, and Ercheng rose against Yao Hong, entered Pingyang, attacked Liyi Yao Chengdu at the Xiongnu fort, raised the Xiongnu Cao Hong as great shanyu, and wherever they went ravaged and plundered.

The original omits 叛泓, the attack on 立義姚成都 at 匈奴堡, and 匈奴曹弘’s identity as great shanyu. The proposal restores those facts, but “Yao Chengdu of Liyi” reads 立義 as a place; it is his title, so the restored sentence should say Liyi Yao Chengdu.

Several tens of thousands of settlements of Hu in Bingzhou, Dingyang, and Ercheng rebelled against Hong and entered Pingyang, attacked and set up Yao Chengdu of Liyi at the Xiongnu fort, pushed Xiongnu Cao Hong as great shanyu, and wherever they went ravaged and plundered.

Several tens of thousands of settlements of Hu in Bingzhou, Dingyang, and Ercheng rebelled against Hong and entered Pingyang, attacked Liyi Yao Chengdu at the Xiongnu fort, pushed the Xiongnu Cao Hong as great shanyu, and wherever they went ravaged and plundered.
攻立義姚成都於匈奴堡 is an attack on titled Liyi Yao Chengdu, not “attacked and set up”; the replacement matches the Chinese.

General Who Conquers the East Yao Yi from Puban campaigned against Hong, fought at Pingyang, greatly defeated him, seized Hong, sent him to Chang'an, and moved fifteen thousand notable settlements to Yongzhou.

General Who Conquers the East Yao Yi from Puban campaigned against Cao Hong, fought at Pingyang, greatly defeated him, seized Cao Hong, sent him to Chang'an, and moved fifteen thousand notable settlements to Yongzhou.
After 推匈奴曹弘為大單于, 討弘 and 執弘 are Cao Hong (弘), not Yao Hong (泓); spelling out Cao Hong removes a real ambiguity.
Yao Zan reached Qinzhou, then withdrew to Chouqi.
贊至秦州，退還仇池 records both reaching Qinzhou and withdrawing to Chouqi; the original keeps only the withdrawal.
Yao Hui quit Anding with five thousand households for Xinping; local leaders blocked him and he galloped alone back to Chang'an.
Yao Hui quit Anding with five thousand households for Xinping; Anding men Hu Yan and Hua Tao blocked him, and he galloped alone back to Chang'an.
安定人胡儼、華韜等 are named blockers, not generic local leaders; the replacement restores both names.
Jianjie Mijie Cheng and Jianwu Pei Qi were killed by Yan; General Who Guards the West Yao Chen abandoned the garrison and fled east.
Lijie Mijie Cheng and Jianwu Pei Qi were killed by Yan; General Who Guards the West Yao Chen abandoned the garrison and fled east.
立節 is Lijie; Jianjie is 建節 from the Wang Zong sentence and is the wrong title here.
Yao Hong sent Lian Mankui and Yao Guang'er to Cangcang; Yang Juan bolted for Sanguan.
Yao Hong sent Lian Mankui and Yao Guang'er to Chencang; Yang Juan bolted for Sanguan.
陳倉 is Chencang; Cangcang is a wrong transcription of the same place-name.
Hong sent General Who Supports the State Lian Mankui and Forward General Yao Guang'er to campaign against Yang Juan at Cangcang; Juan fled to Sanguan.
Hong sent General Who Supports the State Lian Mankui and Forward General Yao Guang'er to campaign against Yang Juan at Chencang; Juan fled to Sanguan.
The same 陳倉 error appears in the literal field; Chencang is the correct reading.
Now he is stranded abroad without voice at court; Anding feels doomed—nine tenths want to flee south. Give him forty thousand veterans and he could drum straight on Chang'an—think of the risk!

Now outside he is cast into a dead place, and inside he does not share court power; the men of Anding think themselves isolated and pressed by the raider—nine houses in ten wish to move south. If he rallies forty thousand crack troops and drums his march on the capital, would that not burden the altars?
若擁精兵四萬 is a hypothetical that Hui himself might rally forty thousand and drum on the capital, not a suggestion that the court give him the troops. The original also drops 死地, 不豫朝權, and 社稷之累.
Yao Yu plotted with Tan Daoji's party; jealous officers smeared Zhao Xuan and pushed Yao Guang to march out.

Yao Guang's Major Yao Yu was in secret communication with Tan Daoji; Chief Clerk Yan Hui, Yang Qian, and others were all Yu's faction, jealous of Zhao Xuan's loyalty; they slandered him together and firmly urged Guang to go out to battle.
主簿閻恢、楊虔等 are named members of Yao Yu’s faction; collapsing them into unnamed jealous officers omits persons the Chinese names.
Jin is inside the passes, four provinces are gone, Bobo tears the west—this is the hour to rally for the throne, not to hoard grain.

The Wu invaders are now inside, four provinces have fallen, western raiders disturb the border, and Qin and Liang have been overthrown—the court's peril is like piled eggs; this is the hour for the lords to rally to the throne.
吳寇內侵 is Wu/Jin invaders striking inward, not “Jin is inside the passes”; 西虜 is unnamed western raiders, not Bobo; 秦、涼覆敗 and 累卵 are in this sentence; “not to hoard grain” belongs to the next sentence.
Yao Yi is dead yet Yao Hui marches on the capital—what now?"
Yi first plotted rebellion and was crushed; Hui again leads hosts in inner revolt—what is to be done?"
懿始構逆滅亡 is that Yi’s rebellion was crushed, not a statement that he is dead; the replacement keeps Hui’s inner revolt and drops the invented death.
Mao Dezu broke Yin Ya at Li, captured him, killed Jin guards, and fled to Tong Pass.
Mao Dezu attacked Hongnong Grand Administrator Yin Ya at Li city; the host broke and Dezu's cavalry seized him; afterward Yin Ya killed the Jin guards and fled to hold Tong Pass.
After 德祖使騎追獲之, 既而殺晉守者奔固潼關 continues Yin Ya as subject; the original wrongly makes Mao Dezu kill the guards and flee.
Tong Pass is the bottleneck; if Yao Shao locks it, Wang Zhen'e is lost.
Tong Pass is Heaven's barrier, a place of advantageous terrain; Zhen'e is an isolated army, his situation perilous and his force small—if Yao Shao is allowed to hold it, he will be hard to deal with.
鎮惡孤軍，勢危力寡，若使姚紹據之，則難圖矣 is a warning that Zhen'e is isolated and Shao holding the pass would be hard to handle, not that Zhen'e is already lost.
Tan Daoji counterattacked but broke and withdrew to Dingcheng.
Tan Daoji led Wang Jing, Shen Linzi, and others in a straight charge at Shao's army; Shao's officers and soldiers were startled and scattered and drew back to Dingcheng.

道濟率王敬、沈林子等逆沖紹軍 is a successful charge; 將士驚散，引還定城, followed by 紹留姚鸞, is Shao’s host withdrawing. The original reverses the defeat. The proposal still names 王敬 as Wang Chong and leaves “the officers and soldiers” unattributed.

Yao Luan sent general Yin Ya against Daoji's major Xu Yan south of Tong Pass; Ya was seized by Yan and sent to Liu Yu.

Wei sent Minister of Education Duke of Nanping Baba Song, straight general Duke of Pingyi Yizhan Juan, and raiding general Wang Luosheng to camp in Hedong as sounding support for Hong.

Yao Chen; Yao Lie of the Vanguard; Yao Bao'an of the Left Guard; Cavalier Attendant Wang Bo; General Who Establishes Martial Might Yao Jin; General Who Displays Might Yao Hao; Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Sun Xuan; and the others all died in battle. The Chinese lists seven named dead and their offices. The revision restores them, renders 建武 as General Who Establishes Martial Might rather than the erroneous 'Jianwei,' and names Yao Hong in the final clause.

建康百里之內，草木皆燋死焉 reports scorched vegetation only; “omen of the tyrant’s fall” is invented commentary.
Yao Chang used Yao Xiang's legacy to seize Chang'an when Fu Jian fell.

The original invents seizing Chang'an. This unit still contains 假容沖之銳，俯定函、秦; the proposal wrongly treats that clause as the next sentence and replaces readable names with unexplained courtesy names. Keep the identifications and restore Hangu and Qin.

剛烈……終表奇節 is a character judgment of sternness and remarkable integrity, not a death scene.

His younger brother Yao Bi plotted to supplant him, yet Yao Hong treated him with unchanged kindness and never showed resentment.
弟 marks Bi as younger, and 奪嫡 concerns the succession.

Yao Shao repeatedly supported Bi, yet Hong trusted Shao wholeheartedly, treated him with the deference due a senior kinsman and bore him no grudge on that account.

Yao Yin, Duke of Nanyang, Grand General Yin Yuan and others plotted rebellion. Yao Hong put them all to death.

After the funeral he took the reins himself, promoted every official a grade, and invited blunt counsel on what helped or hurt the state.

After the burial Hong took charge of government himself and promoted every official at court and in the provinces by one rank. He ordered civil and military officers alike to speak freely about policies unsuited to the times and measures that would bring honor and benefit to the dynasty, holding nothing back.
Hong promotes both central and outside officers and expressly invites criticism from civil and military officials.
Their chief Dang Rong then bolted for home; Yao Hong sent Yao Zan against him.
The Qiang chief Dang Rong then led his followers in revolt and set out for home. Yao Hong sent Pacifying General Yao Zan to attack him.
Dang Rong leads his own followers back in revolt; Yao Zan commands the force against him.

Dang Rong surrendered. Yao Hong moved several hundred of the leading households to Chang’an and sent the rest back to Lirun.

Mao Yong of Beidi seized the Zhao stockade in revolt; Yao Shao captured him.
Mao Yong, governor of Beidi, occupied the Zhao clan’s stockade in revolt against Yao Hong. Yao Shao attacked and captured him.
Mao is governor of Beidi, and his occupation of the clan stronghold is rebellion against Hong.

After the troops had set out, Yao Xuan’s adviser Wei Zong, a deceitful flatterer who delighted in disorder, urged him, “The ruler has only just taken the throne, and his authority is not yet established. Helian Bobo is powerful, and his incursions are sure to cause great harm. Our court’s troubles cannot yet be put to rest.
Wei Zong urges his commander Xuan to act; the speech concerns Bobo's strength and the court's troubles.
You hold the western shield—think hard.
Your Highness has the duty of protecting the ruling house. You should consider this carefully.
維城 evokes the ruling family's protective bulwark; it specifies no western location.
Xingwang is a natural fortress commanding three approaches—seize it in earnest and you secure the west and maybe build a power base."

Xingwang is naturally defensible and commands the approaches from three directions. If you occupy it and govern the people there with an open mind, you can secure your position as a bulwark of the dynasty and even lay the foundations of a hegemon’s or a king’s rule.”
Wei Zong holds out both defense of the dynasty and the prospect of hegemonic or royal power.
Yao Xuan marched thirty-eight thousand households south from Li-run to fortify Xingwang.
Yao Xuan abandoned Lirun and led thirty-eight thousand households south to hold Xingwang.
Xuan abandons Lirun and takes households south to hold Xingwang.

Once Yao Xuan had moved south, the Qiang groups occupied Lirun in revolt. Yao Shao advanced against them and defeated them.

Yao Xuan went to Yao Shao to acknowledge his guilt. Shao killed him in anger.

Earlier, when Yao Xuan was at Xingwang, Yao Hong had sent Yao Fosheng to reason with him. Fosheng ended up supporting Xuan’s plan.

Yao Hong decreed that soldiers who died in royal service should receive posthumous titles and their families should enjoy perpetual exemption from levies.

Yao Zan objected to raising sixteen household officers to noble rank: "The heir's staff owes loyalty by duty—they have done nothing spectacular yet."

Yao Shao stepped forward. “Your Majesty remembers to reward virtue, and you are right to grant them fiefs. In antiquity people treated such matters with reverence, timing the appointments for the beginning of the year. You could wait until next spring and then deliberate.”
